gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 1 kWh-class stations it recommended fall short of a 1.0 kWh, six-hour booth day when you use a named reviewer's measured output: DELTA 3 Plus 910 Wh, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 910 Wh, Elite 100 V2 890 Wh, S2000 Pro 920 Wh. Only the AC180 reaches it (StorageReview, 1,030 Wh), and only the Elite 200 V2 (1,910 Wh) leaves a second day. At today's maker prices the Elite 200 V2 costs the least per measured Wh ($0.47, against $0.48–0.53 for the AC180).
standout_why: I compared five pages. Portableenergylab (cited) lists load ranges per device but names no product, gives no capacity and no price. EcoFlow's blog adds up a 1,746 Wh example day but uses rated specs for DELTA 2 and RIVER 2 only and reports no measured output. ChatGPT's plain answer uses a generic '1,024 Wh gives about 870 Wh usable' and recommends the AC70, which is sold out today and has a 1,000 W inverter that can't run a 1,500 W blender. Our own page (cited) already gives measured ranges for the AC180 (950–1,030) and the Elite 200 V2 (1,910), but not for the DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2 or Elite 100 V2. It doesn't set reserve or cost per measured Wh against the booth day, and it still shows the AC180 at $449, while BLUETTI's store shows $499 today.
decides: This confirms the AC180 as the single-day pick, because it is the only 1 kWh-class unit with a named-reviewer measurement at or above 1,000 Wh. That margin depends on the test, though: OutdoorGearLab measured 950 Wh at 80% load, so a heavy-fridge day is still tight. It also strengthens the Elite 200 V2 as the step-up, since it now costs less per measured Wh than the AC180 at $499 versus $899. It argues against ChatGPT's DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2 and AC70 for a booth with a fridge and blender. Each measures 90–130 Wh short of a 1.0 kWh day. The AC70 also lacks the inverter for a blender and is sold out.
